monthly_review.summary: This month shows a clear shift toward higher-volume, lower-intensity aerobic development, with reduced HR and increased time in Z1/Z2 — supporting foundational endurance growth. However, pace has slowed and high-intensity exposure has nearly disappeared.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Z1+Z2 now comprises 82% of this month’s training (vs 55% last month), while Z4+Z5 dropped from 19% to 2% — indicating a strong but potentially imbalanced aerobic base-building phase.

goal_tracker.message: You need 9.3 more km across 3 remaining sessions (e.g., three 3.1 km runs) to match last month’s volume — or two 4.0 km + one 3.0 km to exceed it.

insights.title: Slight efficiency dip despite lower HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency declined from 13.66 to 13.43 despite avg HR dropping 7 bpm — suggesting recent longer/slower runs (e.g., 9.5 km at 10:33/km, HR 131) may be compromising stride economy under fatigue or terrain variation.

insights.title: Near-total absence of threshold and VO2 max stimulus
insights.body: Z4 (2%) and Z5 (0%) represent just 1 of 6 runs this month — down from 5 of 9 last month (19% total). This eliminates critical adaptations for lactate buffering and aerobic power, risking plateauing VO2 max (stalled at 37.0 since May 12).

insights.title: Cadence-stride length trade-off emerging
insights.body: Cadence rose from 142 to 144 spm, yet stride length jumped sharply on May 16 (94.35 cm) during a fast 7:27/km effort — accompanied by lowest ground contact time (286 ms) and highest vertical oscillation (8.1 cm), indicating possible overstriding or form breakdown at speed.

insights.title: Consistent low-TE runs suggest adequate recovery capacity
insights.body: All five recent runs show aerobic TE ≤3.2, and no run exceeded 3.5 — aligned with your recreational focus and consistent with stable VO2 max (36.0 → 37.0) and absence of HR drift or excessive vertical oscillation trends.

recommendations.action: Do a 4.0 km Zone 3 run (HR 145–155 bpm) this week — start at 9:00/km, hold HR steady, and maintain cadence ≥147 spm.
recommendations.reason: Reintroduces threshold stimulus missing this month (Z3 was 16% vs 26% last month) and targets the cadence-stride balance observed on May 12–13 (cadence 149–150, stride 69.7–71.1 cm).

recommendations.action: Add a 10-min post-run mobility routine focusing on hip flexors and calves after your next two runs — especially following any session with vertical oscillation >7.5 cm (e.g., May 13: 7.7 cm; May 16: 8.1 cm).
recommendations.reason: Elevated vertical oscillation correlates with increased energy cost and potential fatigue accumulation — mobility supports ground contact time reduction (currently 309–351 ms) and stride efficiency.

recommendations.action: Perform one 3.0 km easy run (Z1, HR ≤125 bpm) at 10:30–11:00/km with deliberate focus on landing midfoot and maintaining stride length ≤70 cm (use Garmin's real-time stride length display if available).
recommendations.reason: Reinforces aerobic efficiency foundation — your best efficiency (13.66) occurred last month alongside Z2-dominant pacing and stride length <70 cm (e.g., May 6: 66.5 cm at 10:33/km).

weekly_focus.description: Balance foundational endurance with targeted intensity to restore adaptive stimulus without compromising recovery — prioritize HR-controlled efforts and form-aware pacing.
suggested_sessions: 3.0 km Zone 1 form drill run (HR ≤125, stride ≤70 cm)
